title: French Air Force plans loyal wingman flight in 2028 in sovereign AI push
key_facts: France's Air Force, with the Directorate General for Armament (DGA) and the defense AI agency Amiad, plans to fly crewed fighter jets together with combat drones in 2028 under a project called Hypairion.
Hypairion aims for open, modular aircraft architecture owned by the government and sovereign AI, so France relies less on company-owned systems for critical functions.
Amiad is to provide sovereign AI for command and control and for mission autonomy (AI that helps pilots with mission planning, in-flight decisions and post-mission analysis).
Two Mirage 2000 fighters at Mont-de-Marsan are being modified as AI test beds, with testing starting by the end of the year.
The drone flying in 2028 is a test platform and may not be the future wingman drone planned for the Rafale F5; the first stage may not deliver an operational capability.
The Air Force does not foresee an all-unmanned future; Col. Cedric said the decision to deploy weapons remains human and AI can make mistakes.
The DGA's target date for the first Rafale F5 version is 2033.
quote_evidence: "What Hypairion is really about is equipping the Air Force and our platforms with architectures that are open, modular and owned by the government," Col. Cédric said.
The unmanned aircraft set to fly in 2028 will be a test platform and may not be the future wing-man drone planned for France's Rafale jet.
the decision to deploy weapons remains a human one, and AI can make mistakes.
why_it_matters_hint: France wants the state, not companies, to own the AI and software architecture of its future combat aircraft.
